id.description: Stable plugin identifier and URL slug. Pinned at first submit. For legacy manifests without id, name supplies the identifier.

name.description: Human-readable display name (e.g. "SQLite JDBC"). Without id, this must remain a lowercase slug (1–64 characters) for backwards compatibility.

version.description: Semantic version of this plugin release (no leading "v"). REQUIRED — must match the release tag stripped of any "v" prefix. The registry rejects ingests whose tag and manifest version disagree, so a manifest version bump is the single source of truth for "this is a new release".

description.description: One-line summary shown on the plugin card and search results. Keep it under 280 characters and write it like a tagline, not a paragraph.

category.description: Free-form category label. Used for grouping plugins on the registry home page.

kind.description: Plugin kind slug (must match one of the registry's configured kinds — see the per-kind sections below). Drives which extension fields apply and whether your plugin appears on the catalogue page for that kind.

tags.description: Searchable tags. Used by the registry's search index; max 16 tags, 30 chars each.

license.description: SPDX identifier (e.g. "MIT", "Apache-2.0", "GPL-3.0-only"). Plain text accepted; SPDX is strongly recommended.

icon.description: URL to the plugin icon. Renders next to the plugin name on cards and detail pages. PNG/SVG recommended, 256×256 or vector.

screenshots.description: Up to 12 screenshots shown in the plugin detail gallery.

caption.description: Optional caption shown under the screenshot.

alt.description: Accessible alt text for screen readers.

readme.description: Repo-relative path or URL to the README markdown file. Rendered on the plugin detail page.

readmes.description: Per-locale README overrides. Map keys are BCP-47 locale codes (e.g. "en", "de", "zh-CN"); values are the same shape as `readme`.

documentation_url.description: Link to standalone documentation site (Vitepress, MkDocs, GitHub Pages, etc.). Surfaces as an "Open docs" CTA.

homepage.description: Marketing homepage if separate from the documentation site or the repository.

support.description: Where end users go when they have a problem with the plugin.

min_runtime_version.description: Minimum host runtime version (semver range or single version). The host refuses to load the plugin on older runtimes.

engine.description: Concrete database this driver connects to (e.g. "firestore", "postgres", "qdrant"). Tabularis groups the connection catalogue by engine: every driver targeting the same database shares one engine value, so two "firestore" drivers collapse into a single Firestore entry and the user picks which driver.

paradigms.description: Data-model families the engine supports, most representative first. Single-model drivers declare one (e.g. ["sql"]); multi-model declare several (SurrealDB: ["document","graph","relational","key-value","vector"]). The first entry is the primary model used to place the engine in the catalogue; every entry feeds the filter chips, so a multi-model engine appears when ANY of its models is selected. Allowed values come from the registry's admin-managed paradigm list (facets), not a fixed enum, so new models never need a schema release.

color.description: Hex accent colour shown on the catalogue card and sidebar (e.g. "#f97316").

default_port.description: Default TCP port pre-filled in the connection modal. Omit for file-, folder-, and API-based drivers.

default_username.description: Default username pre-filled in the connection modal (e.g. "postgres", "root").

is_builtin.description: True for drivers shipped with Tabularis. External plugins should omit this or leave it false.

executable.description: Relative path to the plugin executable inside the plugin folder. No extension on Linux/macOS; Tabularis appends .exe on Windows automatically.

interpreter.description: Optional interpreter for script-based plugins (e.g. "python3", "node"). Omit for native binaries.

capabilities.description: Feature flags that control which UI elements Tabularis renders for this driver.

schemas.description: True if the database supports named schemas. Shows the schema selector in the connection UI.

views.description: True to enable the Views section in the database explorer.

routines.description: True to enable stored procedures and functions in the database explorer.

triggers.description: True to enable trigger listing and management.

file_based.description: True for local file databases (e.g. SQLite, DuckDB). Replaces host/port with a file path input.

in_memory.description: Requires file_based. True if the driver also opens the path ":memory:" as a temporary database that lives in the plugin process (e.g. DuckDB). Adds an In-memory shortcut next to the file path input and skips the file existence check for that path.

folder_based.description: True for plugins that connect to a directory rather than a single file (e.g. CSV).

connection_string.description: Set false to hide the connection-string import UI for this driver.

connection_string_example.description: Optional placeholder example shown in the connection-string field (e.g. "postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/db").

identifier_quote.description: Character used to quote SQL identifiers: double-quote for ANSI SQL, backtick for MySQL-style.

alter_primary_key.description: True if the database supports altering primary keys after table creation.

auto_increment_keyword.description: Keyword appended after the column type for auto-increment columns (e.g. "AUTO_INCREMENT" for MySQL).

serial_type.description: Replacement data type used for auto-increment columns (e.g. "SERIAL" for PostgreSQL).

inline_pk.description: True if the primary key is defined inline in the column definition (e.g. SQLite AUTOINCREMENT).

alter_column.description: True if the driver supports ALTER TABLE MODIFY/ALTER COLUMN on existing tables.

create_foreign_keys.description: True if the driver properly supports creating foreign key constraints.

no_connection_required.description: True for API-based plugins that need no host/port/credentials (e.g. public REST APIs).

single_database.description: Driver exposes a single implicit database (e.g. a flat search/document store like Meilisearch). Skips the database tab and the database-name field in the connection modal.

manage_tables.description: True if the driver supports table and column management (CREATE/ALTER/DROP). Defaults to true.

readonly.description: When true, the driver is read-only: INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE are disabled in the UI.

materialized_views.description: True if the driver supports materialized views (e.g. PostgreSQL). When false, Tabularis skips fetching them entirely.

routine_management.description: True if stored routines can be run with parameters, created from a template, edited and dropped. Distinct from `routines`, which only lists them.

explain.description: True if the driver supports EXPLAIN / query plans. When false, the Visual Explain UI is hidden for connections using this driver.

supports_ssl.description: True to show the SSL/TLS tab (mode plus CA / client certificate / key) in the connection modal. This is where Tabularis reads the flag — the top-level `supports_ssl` field is legacy and ignored by the host.

sql_dialect.description: SQL dialect for the statement splitter and classifier: string-literal quoting, identifier quoting, dollar-quoted strings, DELIMITER / GO directives. Omitting the field falls back to "postgres".

connection_uri.description: True if the driver consumes the raw connection URI verbatim instead of the decomposed host/port/database fields. Set this when the scheme carries semantics the decomposition would destroy — e.g. the DNS seedlist lookup implied by `mongodb+srv://`, whose hosts publish SRV records but no A record.

connection_uri_schemes.description: Additional URI schemes this driver handles, beyond its own id and the scheme of `connection_string_example` (e.g. ["mongodb+srv"]). A declared scheme never displaces one another driver already owns.

table_query_templates.description: True if the driver provides SQL templates for SELECT, UPDATE and DELETE.

column_comments.description: True if the driver can store a description per column. Shows a Description input in the column editor and sends it as `comment` in ColumnDefinition.

sql_syntax.description: Declarative SQL syntax extending a preset, for engines no preset describes (e.g. GoogleSQL). Data only. Every field is optional and overrides one rule of the extended preset; invalid fields are ignored with a warning and never fail loading. Hosts that predate it ignore it and use sql_dialect. See PLUGIN_GUIDE.md#sql-syntax-sql_syntax.

extends.description: Preset to extend. Defaults to sql_dialect.

quotes.description: Replaces the preset's quote rules; each open at most once.

close.description: Defaults to open (] for [); any other value is invalid.

escape.description: double: '' escapes a quote; backslash: \' (no doubling); both; none.

triple_quoted_strings.description: '''…''' and """…""" strings for the ' and " string quotes.

string_prefixes.description: Letter prefixes before a string quote, any case (e.g. r, b, rb, br).

line_comment_requires_space.description: -- needs a following whitespace to start a comment.

script_blocks.description: Procedural BEGIN … END, IF, LOOP, WHILE, REPEAT, FOR and CASE blocks stay one statement.

string_escape.description: How generated string literals are escaped: standard ('') or backslash (\').

like_escape.description: Whether LIKE … ESCAPE is supported. false: LIKE filters escape wildcards with a backslash and omit ESCAPE.

boolean_literals.description: How Tabularis writes boolean literals in SQL it generates (dumps, Copy as INSERT, filters, notebook cell references). keywords: TRUE / FALSE. numeric: 1 / 0. Omit to keep each generator's default (dumps: TRUE / FALSE on postgres, 1 / 0 elsewhere). Set keywords for an engine without implicit integer-to-boolean coercion (GoogleSQL).

drop_table_sql.description: The explorer's Drop table action asks the optional get_drop_table_sql RPC for the statement. Without it the generic DROP TABLE is used and the RPC is never called.

data_files.description: Requires file_based. Data file formats (csv, tsv, json, ndjson, parquet, xlsx) the driver exposes as a queryable relation through the optional open_data_file RPC.

settings.description: Optional list of configuration fields the plugin exposes to the user via the Tabularis settings modal.

options.description: Allowed values, used only when type is "select".

data_types.description: List of data types this driver supports for column creation in the UI.

name.description: Type name as it appears in DDL (e.g. "VARCHAR", "BIGINT").

category.description: UI grouping category. Mirrors the category values used by Tabularis built-in drivers.

requires_length.description: True if this type requires a length argument (e.g. VARCHAR(255)).

requires_precision.description: True if this type requires a precision/scale argument (e.g. DECIMAL(10,2)).

default_length.description: Optional default length value pre-filled in the UI.

supports_ssl.description: true to show the SSL/TLS configuration tab (mode + CA/client cert/key) in the connection modal for this network driver. Defaults to false.

ui_extensions.description: UI extension contributions rendered into named slots of the Tabularis interface. Only needed by plugins that ship a frontend module; driver-only plugins omit it.

module.description: Module path relative to the plugin directory (e.g. "dist/index.js").

order.description: Ordering weight when several plugins contribute to the same slot; lower renders earlier.

driver.description: Restrict the contribution to a single driver id. Omit to render for every driver.

type_mappings.description: Optional map of generic inferred type names to driver-native types, resolved by the host during paste/import (map_inferred_type). Keys are uppercase generic names (e.g. DATETIME, JSON); values are the driver-native equivalents (e.g. TIMESTAMP, JSONB). Lookup is case-insensitive; unmapped types pass through unchanged.

explain_parsers.description: Plugin-owned raw EXPLAIN parser IIFE bundles loaded by Tabularis when the plugin is enabled.

engine.description: Canonical database engine identifier handled by this parser.

format.description: Globally unique raw EXPLAIN wire-format tag.

module.description: Path to the parser IIFE relative to the installed plugin directory.

label.description: Optional human-readable label for format pickers.

connection_metadata.description: Opt in to get_connection_metadata, which returns connection-specific capabilities, data_types and type_mappings. Static manifest values remain the fallback.

connection_fields.description: Optional presentation overrides for host-owned connection fields. Omitted fields keep the standard Tabularis behavior.
